row.evidence: ThoughtSpot's docs say SCIM 2.0 provisioning is enabled by default for a cluster, but neither the pricing page (Essentials $25, Pro $50, Enterprise custom) nor the editions docs say which plan includes it.
row.notes: Status unknown: SCIM is documented but not tied to any of the three public plans (rule 1a). SAML/OIDC SSO is ticked for Pro and Enterprise only on the pricing table. SCIM deprovisioning is a hard delete (content moves to tsadmin), so scim_ops.deactivate is false. SCIM tokens expire after six months. REST API v2 has user activate/deactivate endpoints; the plan that unlocks it is not stated (the pricing page sells 'Embedded for internal enterprise applications (API & SDK)' as an Enterprise add-on).

auth.token_source: Admin portal > All Orgs > Authentication > Provisioning > Generate Token (per-Org tokens from each Org's Admin > Security settings)

deprovision.data_retained: Hard delete, no suspended state; the user's Liveboards, saved Answers and scheduled jobs transfer to tsadmin. Re-provisioning creates a new account and content is not reassigned automatically.

roles.how: IdP group membership syncs to ThoughtSpot groups, which carry role privileges

limitations.text: Deactivation in the IdP (Okta deactivate, Entra disable or unassign) results in a permanent delete; there is no soft-deactivated state.
Large change volumes take 20 to 40 minutes to appear.
SAML group mapping overrides SCIM group assignments on login; do not enable both.
Multi-Org instances need a separate IdP SCIM app and Org-scoped token per Org; enabling SCIM per Org requires ThoughtSpot support.

endpoints.purpose: Update a group, add/remove users and privileges

limitations.text: Audit log fetch needs the ADMINISTRATION privilege.

okta.notes: OIN page marks OIDC, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Sync Password, Group Push and Schema Discovery as checked (read from page markup); SAML not checked.

entra.notes: ThoughtSpot points to Microsoft's generic SCIM provisioning docs; no ThoughtSpot tutorial found at learn.microsoft.com (thoughtspot-provisioning-tutorial and thoughtspot-tutorial return 404).

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: By default, SCIM is enabled for a cluster. If your ThoughtSpot instance uses Orgs, you must enable SCIM at the Org level to ensure that users are provisioned to a particular group in a particular Org. To enable SCIM per Org, contact ThoughtSpot support.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Before you configure, ensure that your IdP supports SCIM 2.0 for a seamless integration with ThoughtSpot.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Click Generate Token to generate and copy the authentication token. This token is used to authenticate the SCIM service (ThoughtSpot application) in your IdP.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Each SCIM token has a validity of only six months.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: ThoughtSpot supports create, read, update, and delete of users and groups, and provisioning users to groups within Orgs.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: ThoughtSpot's SCIM implementation treats a de-provisioning request as a permanent (hard) delete.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: When a user is removed from ThoughtSpot through SCIM de-provisioning, their content — including personal Liveboards, saved Answers, and scheduled jobs — is automatically transferred to the tsadmin user. No content is deleted.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: ThoughtSpot does not support a suspended or soft-deactivated user state. When a de-provisioning signal is received, users are permanently deleted.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Membership in a group in the IdP can automatically assign the corresponding role in ThoughtSpot, controlling access levels.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Low volume changes made in IdP may be reflected immediately in ThoughtSpot. Larger volume changes are usually reflected within 20 to 40 minutes.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Avoid enabling both SAML group mapping and SCIM provisioning simultaneously, as SAML group mapping will override SCIM group assignments on user login.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM
citations.quote: Copy the token from ThoughtSpot in the bearer token field provided in the Okta interface.

citations.title: Manage users and groups with SCIM

citations.title: Configure SCIM for multi-Org deployments
